title: The Blade Itself
author: Joe Abercrombie
summary: A crippled torturer, an arrogant young noble fencer and a barbarian warrior who wants to be left alone are all caught up when a wizard arrives and a war in the north draws near. None of them is a hero in the usual sense.
readIf: you like grim, funny, cynical fantasy where characters are flawed and the fights are brutal.
skipIf: you want inspiring heroes or a tidy, self-contained story, as this starts a trilogy with a slow build.

pairings.reason: Another darkly funny, sharply written fantasy with deeply imperfect leads.
Another epic where politics are brutal and the good guys do not always win.
A gritty, soldier's-eye fantasy with the same refusal to romanticise war.
